metadata.title: David Thompson Thai Food - Red Curry Paste

David Thompson making Curry.
He's cooking Red curry, Green curry, Massaman and Chili jam

More information, please visit : http://www.davidthompsonthaifood.com

nodes.plm_caption:
This video shows a chef preparing an ingredients on a stainless steel kitchen counter top. He uses a mortar and pestle and a round cutting board.
The chef picks up a red, long chili and talks about it while he holds it in his hands before chopping it up quickly with a knife on the circular chopping board. He also chops up a red onion before piling up the ingredients. He pats them together and then takes some of them and adds them to the mortar, which he grinds them with pestle. He then adds more, continues to grind, and pushes out the finished product. He talks about the finished product before the video cuts to the end screen, and the word 'Curry' is written in white in the middle of the screen.

This is a good example of how to make your own curry in a restaurant kitchen. It is an excellent video for kitchen staff to watch if they want to learn how to make curry.

summary.brief: A chef chops chilies, onion and aromatics, then pounds them with spices in a mortar to make red curry paste.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a male chef in a white coat standing at a stainless‑steel counter surrounded by bowls of ingredients. He removes the seeds from dried red chilies, soaks the chilies in water, squeezes out the excess liquid and chops the softened chilies together with red shallots, garlic, lemongrass and lime zest on a round cutting board. The chopped pieces are transferred to a mortar, where he adds a small amount of shrimp paste, dried spices such as coriander seed, cumin seed, white pepper, nutmeg and a pinch of salt. Using the pestle he repeatedly pounds and scrapes the mixture, adding the remaining aromatics until the blend becomes a smooth, fine red paste. He then scoops the finished paste into a bowl, shows it to the camera while commenting on its texture, and the video ends with an end‑screen that displays the word “Curry.”

action.brief: Pound ingredients into red curry paste
action.detailed: Chop the seeded, soaked chilies with shallots, garlic, lemongrass and lime zest, add shrimp paste and the dried spices, place everything into a mortar, and repeatedly pound with the pestle until a smooth red curry paste forms, then transfer the paste to a serving bowl.
action.actor: Male chef wearing a white coat and apron

nodes.plm_caption: The video captures a male chef making a red curry dish in a commercial kitchen. The chef can be seen moving around the kitchen and interacting with ingredients.

summary.brief: The chef presents the ingredient bowls, then removes seeds, peels, squeezes, slices and chops red chilies for the curry paste.
summary.detailed: A male chef dressed in a white coat stands at a stainless‑steel counter surrounded by a row of small white bowls containing red chilies, onions, garlic, cilantro, lime, chives and other aromatics. He points to each bowl while naming the ingredients. He then picks up a long red chili, cuts it with a knife, removes its seeds into a separate white dish and places the flesh in another. Repeating this with several chilies, he squeezes out excess moisture over a bowl, peels or strips the skins, slices the peppers on a round wooden cutting board, and finally chops the slices into fine pieces that fall into a bowl, all while the other ingredient bowls remain visible in the background.

action.detailed: Remove the seeds from each red chili, peel or strip the flesh, squeeze out excess water, slice the peppers on the wooden board, and then chop the slices into small pieces, depositing the results into bowls.
action.actor: A male chef wearing a white coat and apron

summary_sent_to_llm.title: David Thompson Thai Food - Red Curry Paste
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
David Thompson making Curry.
He's cooking Red curry, Green curry, Massaman and Chili jam

More information, please visit : http://www.davidthompsonthaifood.com
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a male chef in a white coat standing at a stainless‑steel counter surrounded by bowls of ingredients. He removes the seeds from dried red chilies, soaks the chilies in water, squeezes out the excess liquid and chops the softened chilies together with red shallots, garlic, lemongrass and lime zest on a round cutting board. The chopped pieces are transferred to a mortar, where he adds a small amount of shrimp paste, dried spices such as coriander seed, cumin seed, white pepper, nutmeg and a pinch of salt. Using the pestle he repeatedly pounds and scrapes the mixture, adding the remaining aromatics until the blend becomes a smooth, fine red paste. He then scoops the finished paste into a bowl, shows it to the camera while commenting on its texture, and the video ends with an end‑screen that displays the word “Curry.”

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
